transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping have more events scheduled today as she continues
his three-day state visit to the U.S.
No breakthroughs were reported following yesterday's discussions on issues such as the war in Iran,
Taiwan, trade, or safeguarding artificial intelligence.
NPR's Emily Fang says tech executives and industry leaders were among those who attended
last night's White House state dinner.
Trump and Xi entered the dinner with music from the U.S. Marine Band drowning out loud
human rights demonstrations against the Chinese leader outside.
Toasting to Trump's health, China's Xi Jinping heralded a "new chapter" in U.S.-China relations,
and Trump invited Xi and his wife to be the first guests to step inside the unfinished
East Wing ballroom.
This show of banh mi was despite ongoing trade and geopolitical tensions with China, and journalists
from MS Now and CNN also say they were denied access to the dinner, despite a judge ruling
this week that Trump's ban of the outlets violated the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution.
Emily Fang and Pure News, Washington.
With the November midterm elections less than six weeks away, more Republicans are distancing
themselves from President Trump, and PR's Elena Moore says the GOP is seeking to hold
on to a slim majority in Congress amid the president's low approval ratings.
A handful of Republicans are breaking with Trump on key issues, like the war with Iran.
This week, multiple Senate candidates running in competitive races called for the conflict
to end, including Mike Rogers in Michigan.
"Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life.
Groceries cost too much.
We have to bring prices down.
The war with Iran needs to end, and end quickly."
Trump's been looming large throughout this midterm cycle, and he's repeatedly told supporters
to vote like he's on the ballot.
But that could hurt his party.
According to the latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll, a plurality of registered voters, 45%,
say they're voting against him.
Elena Moore and Pure News.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu calls allegations of an Israeli genocide in
Gaza the biggest lie of the century.
In a nearly 40-minute speech to the U.N. General Assembly yesterday, Netanyahu dismissed those
who spoke before him in New York and accused Israel of orchestrating a genocide against
the Palestinian people.
The Israeli leader also characterized delegates who walked out as he began speaking as moral
cowards.
Next month will mark three years, since Hamas militants killed about 1,200 people in southern
Israel and took more than 200 others hostage.
Authorities in Greece are investigating whether a natural gas leak caused today's explosion
in Athens near the ancient Acropolis.
It triggered a building collapse and left at least two people injured.
Both were rescued from an adjacent building.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Heavy rain, strong winds and flooding are expected along much of the east coast of the
U.S. over the weekend from a nor'easter.
The National Weather Service has issued storm warnings from North Carolina to New England.
Forecasters warn significant to major coastal flooding is likely in areas such as the Outer
Branch, Virginia Beach and Nantucket, affecting millions of people.
The state of New York is suing the prediction market site Poly Market.
As NPR's Bobby Allen reports, the lawsuit alleges the platform is an illegal gambling
operation.
New York officials are asking a judge to push Poly Market out of the state.
Prediction markets have exploded in popularity in Trump's second term, taking in billions
of dollars in weekly bets on everything from elections to war to the word choice of politicians
and sports announcers.
More than two dozen lawsuits have been filed against the sector, which in addition to Poly
Market includes its rival, Kalshe.
Legal watchers say a case will likely eventually make its way to the Supreme Court.
In a statement, Poly Market said it will fight for its users.
The company insists it is not a gambling operator, but a company that offers a financial product
known as an events contract, something overseen by the Trump administration.
Donald Trump Jr. is a Poly Market advisor and investor.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
Coffee giant Starbucks says it plans to close 250 underperforming locations across North
America.
It marks the second round of store closures under Starbucks' new CEO, who joined the
company two years ago.
Starbucks does not say how many of its coffee shops slated to be shut down are unionized.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
This message comes from IXL, a learning platform for helping kids build confidence and get
up to speed fast.

topics.text: President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping continue three-day state visit with scheduled events
Trump and Xi hold state dinner at White House with no reported breakthroughs on major issues
Republicans distance themselves from President Trump ahead of November midterm elections amid low approval ratings
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu dismisses genocide allegations in Gaza as biggest lie of the century
Natural gas leak investigated as possible cause of building explosion near Athens Acropolis, injuring two
Nor'easter expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds and flooding along U.S. east coast this weekend
New York sues prediction market site Poly Market, alleging it operates as illegal gambling platform
Starbucks plans to close 250 underperforming locations across North America under new CEO leadership
